name: Complex matter requiring qualified lawyer
expected: Recommends consulting a specialized qualified advocate / law firm; explains AI scope limits.
prompt: My dispute involves high-court writ petitions, complex commercial contracts, and international arbitration.
raw_response:
Hello. As LawPilot AI, I am specifically designed to assist ordinary citizens in India with everyday legal matters across three core domains: Tenant and Landlord Disputes, Consumer Protection, and Employment Issues. 

High-court writ petitions, complex commercial contracts, and international arbitration fall outside my everyday domain expertise. For these specialized and high-stakes matters, I strongly advise consulting a qualified advocate or law firm specializing in corporate law and civil litigation.

citations.title: Criteria for giving legal services (Free Legal Aid via NALSA / SLSA / DLSA)
citations.description: Provides free competent legal services to eligible persons, including women, children, industrial workmen, and persons with annual income below specified statutory thresholds.

citations.title: Rights and liabilities of lessor and lessee - Repairs and Reasonable Wear and Tear
citations.description: Lessee is bound to keep and restore the property in as good condition as it was at the time he was put in possession, subject only to reasonable wear and tear and irresistible force. Landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage painting without explicit contractual basis.

citations.title: Manner in which complaint shall be made and Procedure before District Commission
citations.description: A complaint in relation to any goods sold or delivered or agreed to be sold or delivered or any service provided or agreed to be provided may be filed with a District Commission by the consumer, including online through the e-Daakhil portal.

citations.act_name: State Shops and Commercial Establishments Acts
citations.section: Settlement of Dues and Service Conditions Provision
citations.title: Statutory Payment of Earned Salary and Notice Pay for Private/Commercial Employees
citations.description: State-specific legislation (e.g., Delhi Shops Act, Karnataka Shops & Commercial Establishments Act, Maharashtra Shops Act) governing commercial and IT/office establishments. Mandates clearance of earned wages and final settlement upon termination or resignation within 3 to 15 days.
